## Task T14 (narrative: work/T14/report.md)

### Arguments (5)

#### A-T14-001 — Enduring significance: necessity versus enhancement (position: Positive conditional reconstruction)

- Premises: Relationships, understanding and achieved goods can be worth preserving., Specified continuation retains the same subjects and relevant goods., Additional worthwhile experience is available without overriding harm.
- Bridge principles: Comparative enhancement needs a defensible value ordering., Necessity additionally needs total loss to defeat all significance in the selected domain.
- Conclusion: Endurance can enhance significance under these premises; necessity and actuality require more.
- Claims: CL-T14-001, CL-T14-002, CL-T14-007, CL-T14-010, CL-T14-011, CL-T14-013; sources: S-T14-001, S-T14-004
- Strongest objection: Finite goods may retain value even when no one later remembers; endless continuation may damage what mattered.; strongest reply: A defender can argue continued shared life is an additional relational good, not merely a record, while defending separately the stronger non-loss requirement.
- Unresolved issues: Value ordering; whose goods; identity; extent of duration; no inferred actual survival
- Review: R14 (accept)

#### A-T14-002 — Finite value with an acknowledged cosmic remainder (position: Finite-value countercase)

- Premises: A finite instance of learning, care or relief can benefit actual subjects., The worth of that benefit need not depend entirely on subsequent recognition.
- Bridge principles: Non-erasure principle: later absence alone does not retroactively make every earlier benefit worthless.
- Conclusion: Finite meaning can be real on this account while cosmic intention and enduring significance remain separate questions.
- Claims: CL-T14-003, CL-T14-004, CL-T14-009, CL-T14-011; sources: S-T14-002
- Strongest objection: A meaningful episode may still lack an ultimately worthwhile setting; all loss can defeat the hoped-for relationship to a larger whole.; strongest reply: Distinguish missing further goods from nonexistence of prior goods; do not claim this answers the larger purpose question.
- Unresolved issues: Ground of objective value; relation of local to whole-life value; criterion of ultimate significance
- Review: R14 (accept)

#### A-T14-003 — Williams on categorical desire and immortal life, with Fischer’s reply (position: Inspected original challenge and reply, with project adjudication)

- Premises: Williams: categorical desires can give present reasons to continue, independently of merely avoiding frustration., Williams: an adequate immortal prospect must preserve the person and relate appropriately to the aims motivating survival., Williams argues extended fixed-character life undermines motivation, while disjoint or radically accumulated lives fail to solve the appropriate-relation problem.
- Bridge principles: The author’s modal step generalizes from conditions of recognizably human character to endless human existence; this remains contested., A burden about appropriate prospective concern is distinct from numerical identity and from objective worth.
- Conclusion: Williams supplies a stronger challenge than mere hedonic boredom, but its universal necessity is not established by the present comparison; conditional worthwhile endurance remains open.
- Claims: CL-T14-005, CL-T14-006, CL-T14-010, CL-T14-012, CL-T14-013, CL-T14-019, CL-T14-020; sources: S-T14-007, S-T14-003
- Strongest objection: Fischer allows varied activities, appropriately spaced repeatable pleasures, and acceptable character development; absorbed attention need not eliminate ownership. These contest inevitable exhaustion and indiscriminate identity-loss claims.; strongest reply: A strengthened Williams-side response asks whether renewal preserves genuine engagement and prospective reasons rather than simply suppressing awareness of impoverishment. Occasional pleasantness does not settle that question, and every experience being owned does not by itself establish an adequate relation to present aims.
- Unresolved issues: Whether human categorical projects necessarily exhaust under all relevant immortal arrangements Whether relational development can renew motivation while preserving identity and appropriate concern Fischer’s repeatability/variety response does not alone establish objective worth or infinite resources Williams addresses endless human life; application to strict timeless foundation or transformed persons needs additional premises
- Review: R14 (accept)

#### A-T14-004 — Cosmic purpose and normative worth (position: Strong purpose account with bridge audit)

- Premises: An agent intends a stated end for a specified cosmic domain., Its causal or grounding contribution explains why that domain has relevant features., The end and agent-person relation are normatively worthwhile.
- Bridge principles: Intentional explanation requires independent warrant for intention and constraints., Authorship supplies a purpose relation, not worth by definition.
- Conclusion: A worthy intentional relation can add cosmic significance conditionally; observed conscious production alone does not establish it.
- Claims: CL-T14-002, CL-T14-008, CL-T14-014, CL-T14-015, CL-T14-016; sources: S-T14-001, S-T14-004
- Strongest objection: Arbitrary or harmful ends would still be purposes; a timeless agent model owes coherent intention; designer premises remain unsupported.; strongest reply: Specify a loving creator-person relation and whole-history intention, or temporal agency; assess these with the same standards as rival primitive laws and value commitments.
- Unresolved issues: Actual intention; agency model; normative foundation; domain; goodness and authority deferred
- Review: R14 (accept)

#### A-T14-005 — Consciousness-factory discrimination (position: Comparative model design)

- Premises: Production, development and preservation are different proposed ends., Each end is paired with a declared population, means, constraints and tradeoffs.
- Bridge principles: Outcomes weaken a model only when excluded or disfavored by those fixed commitments., Observer selection and shared premises must be included.
- Conclusion: Precisely constrained variants can face qualitative tests; unrestricted hidden purposes discriminate weakly.
- Claims: CL-T14-015, CL-T14-016, CL-T14-017, CL-T14-018; sources: —
- Strongest objection: Unknown goals/resources can accommodate almost any outcome; conscious observers necessarily observe from a conscious perspective.; strongest reply: Precommit to independent goals, inclusion rules and feasible alternatives; compare the same data across intentional, impersonal-teleological and incidental models.
- Depends on arguments: A-T14-004
- Unresolved issues: No population survey or likelihoods; no completed test; suffering analysis deferred to T15
- Review: R14 (accept)

## Task P2T13 (narrative: work/P2T13/report.md)

### Arguments (3)

#### A-P2T13-001 — Final loss and the necessity of endurance (position: Reconstructed strict necessity rationale; neither Yoshizawa nor Metz endorses its soundness)

- Premises: Ordinary relationships and activities can be valuable., Death ends a person and may end valued relationships., The strict advocate claims the ending makes the whole life meaningless.
- Bridge principles: Ending must negate relevant whole-life significance, not merely preclude additional goods., The meaning at issue and its temporal bearer must be specified.
- Conclusion: The third premise would require endurance for meaning only if the loss-to-meaninglessness bridge is defended.
- Claims: CL-P2T13-001, CL-P2T13-002, CL-P2T13-003, CL-P2T13-004, CL-P2T13-008, CL-P2T13-009, CL-P2T13-010, CL-P2T13-023; sources: S-P2T13-002, S-T14-004
- Strongest objection: Yoshizawa distinguishes no existing subject from an existing subject without meaning, and past meaning from present instantiation; strict necessity does not follow from an ending.; strongest reply: Metz reformulates the strict rationale to avoid conceding finite meaning, then questions whether endless retention avoids ideal value; his hypothetical further response separates perfection from explanatory work.
- Unresolved issues: The selected 2013 original remains unavailable. No later author summary or critic replaces that missing inspection. Yoshizawa’s Tolstoy reconstruction is not verified historical intention. Final-loss concern is neither merely boredom nor settled by labelling the desired good perfect.
- Review: P2R13 (accept)

#### A-P2T13-002 — Possible worthwhile continuation with ownership and engagement (position: Conditional enhancement; no necessity/sufficiency/actuality conclusion)

- Premises: Some activities can remain worthwhile or repeatable., A future life can contain varied goods and changes acceptable through reflection., The future experiences must belong to the same person and remain appropriately attractive.
- Bridge principles: Finite repeatability must extend to the proposed duration., Future subjectivity and identity must actually obtain for survival., Possible appeal does not establish all endless lives good.
- Conclusion: A coherent worthwhile continuation may enhance a life, while finite meaning and actual survival remain separate questions.
- Claims: CL-P2T13-013, CL-P2T13-014, CL-P2T13-017, CL-P2T13-018, CL-P2T13-019, CL-P2T13-020, CL-P2T13-021, CL-P2T13-024; sources: S-T14-003, S-T14-002
- Strongest objection: Williams’s stronger concern is exhausted categorical projects or a remote life not appropriately related to the present person; ordinary repetition may fail indefinitely.; strongest reply: Fischer distinguishes repeatable from self-exhausting goods, permits a varied life and appropriate character changes, and separates absorption from ownership.
- Unresolved issues: Williams original is frozen accepted derivative, not fresh reading. No infinite aggregate-value measure, empirical immortality or survival inference. Fischer exact proof-to-final and journal collation unresolved.
- Review: P2R13 (accept)

#### A-P2T13-003 — Finite value, ultimate context and intended purpose (position: Several conditional questions; no forced metaphysical winner)

- Premises: Worthwhile engagement can be evaluated at the level of an individual life., Cosmic role or ultimate context asks additional questions., Intended purpose requires agency/end/grounding; worthwhile purpose requires normative justification.
- Bridge principles: Local worth must not silently become an answer to every ultimate-context concern., Descriptive occurrence must not become intention., A divine theory’s possibility is distinct from its actuality or necessity.
- Conclusion: Finite value and possible divine/enduring enhancement can be compared without deriving purpose, perfect goodness or actual continuation.
- Claims: CL-P2T13-011, CL-P2T13-012, CL-P2T13-013, CL-P2T13-015, CL-P2T13-016, CL-P2T13-025, CL-P2T13-026, CL-P2T13-027, CL-P2T13-028, CL-P2T13-029, CL-P2T13-030, CL-P2T13-031, CL-P2T13-032; sources: S-T14-002, S-T14-004, S-P2T13-003
- Strongest objection: An advocate may argue all finite value requires divine grounding or that ultimate loss defeats local significance.; strongest reply: Wolf identifies finite fitting engagement but expressly limits cosmic solace; Metz concedes limited force of his timeless-purpose challenge in the 2015 selectedpassage. The 2000 original itself already leaves two response strategies open and does not claim the objection requires disbelief (p311).
- Unresolved issues: Metz 2000 exact original repaired; direct 2007 Affolter/Metzreply bodies remain deferred. Exact 2013 selectedchapter unavailable. Affolter 2007 and Poettckeroriginals deferred; no fabricateddirectreplycoverage. Objectivevaluegrounding, humanidentity and timelessmind remain unresolved.

- Review: P2R13 (accept)

#### CL-P2T13-020 [philosophical_premise]

Fischer distinguishes self-exhausting from repeatable pleasures, relative to a person and their distribution, and proposes that repeatable goods may sustain categorical desires.

- Sources: S-T14-003 (pp230–235;§IVp237)
- Dependency group: DG-P2T13-S-T14-003
- Reliability: directly_inspected_attribution; inference strength: contested
- Limitations: Extrapolation to unending life and the relation of pleasure to meaning remain contestable; no measured immortal sample.
- Review: P2R13 (accept)

#### CL-P2T13-021 [philosophical_premise]

Fischer permits changes of character arising through appropriate reflection to remain attractive, while distinguishing coercion, deception and other unwelcome changes.

- Sources: S-T14-003 (p236)
- Dependency group: DG-P2T13-S-T14-003
- Reliability: directly_inspected_attribution; inference strength: contested
- Limitations: Finite analogies do not resolve every indefinitely extended identity or present-concern case.
- Review: P2R13 (accept)

#### CL-P2T13-022 [source_version_provenance]

The inspected Fischer review copy is a later reprint layout, not the 1994 journal layout: its pages are224–238 and its apparatus includes an editorial 1996 publication note and a 2004 translation.

- Sources: S-T14-003 (p. 225 n. 11; p238references; primary 1994 metadata Q012R001; Broadview metadata Q008R001)
- Dependency group: DG-P2T13-S-T14-003
- Reliability: directly_inspected_attribution; inference strength: conditional
- Limitations: Broadview 2009 anthology is a supported candidate; exact proof-to-final and journal collation remains unresolved. PDF 2022 dates do not date the argument.
- Review: P2R13 (accept)

#### CL-P2T13-023 [inference]

The selected final-loss exchange does not establish that ending a life erases its earlier value; treating absence as an existing state without meaning requires a further bridge.

- Sources: S-P2T13-002 (Yoshizawap146nn18–19;Metz 2015§3.1pp253–254), S-T14-004
- Dependency group: DG-P2T13-project-bridges
- Reliability: directly_inspected_attribution; inference strength: conditional
- Supporting claims: CL-P2T13-003, CL-P2T13-008, CL-P2T13-009, CL-P2T13-010
- Limitations: The strongest strict necessity advocate can dispute retrospective attribution; the present packet does not settle every theory of value or time.
- Review: P2R13 (accept)

#### CL-P2T13-024 [inference]

Possible worthwhile continuation requires relevant goods, an appropriate relation to the person, and actual further experience before it can support a personal-survival claim.

- Sources: S-T14-003 (Fischerpp224–227,235–237; frozen T13CL016–019and T14CL010,013)
- Dependency group: DG-P2T13-project-bridges
- Reliability: directly_inspected_attribution; inference strength: conditional
- Supporting claims: CL-P2T13-017, CL-P2T13-018, CL-P2T13-020, CL-P2T13-021
- Limitations: Information, recognition and a complete history can preserve something valuable without supplying further subjectivity. No new empirical survival evidence.
- Review: P2R13 (accept)

#### CL-P2T13-025 [inference]

An occurrence of consciousness, an intended role, and a worthy role remain distinct claims; duration or value alone establishes none of the agency, intention and normative bridges.

- Sources: S-T14-004 (Metz 2015 pp255–257;Wolfpp8–10,33; frozen T14CL015–018), S-T14-002
- Dependency group: DG-P2T13-project-bridges
- Reliability: directly_inspected_attribution; inference strength: conditional
- Supporting claims: CL-P2T13-012, CL-P2T13-013, CL-P2T13-016
- Limitations: No creator purpose, goodness, authority or metaphysical family winner is established.
- Review: P2R13 (accept)

#### CL-P2T13-026 [philosophical_premise]

Yoshizawa explicitly distinguishes the four-dimensional existence of a finite life from eternity or transcending temporality.

- Sources: S-P2T13-002 (p. 147 n. 20)
- Dependency group: DG-P2T13-S-P2T13-002
- Reliability: directly_inspected_attribution; inference strength: contested
- Limitations: His Singer quotation is not an independent inspection of Singer; neither eternalism nor a timeless conscious bearer is established.
- Review: P2R13 (accept)

#### CL-P2T13-027 [philosophical_premise]

Metz 2000 defines purpose theory as a conditional account of what could confer meaning, not a claim that God or an assigned purpose actually exists. It can permit meaning without an afterlife.

- Sources: S-P2T13-003 (pp293–295)
- Dependency group: DG-P2T13-Metz-purpose
- Reliability: directly_inspected_attribution; inference strength: contested
- Limitations: Purpose theory is distinct from justice/perfection theories; no existence or survival inference.
- Review: P2R13 (accept)

#### CL-P2T13-028 [philosophical_premise]

Metz 2000 distinguishes a purpose assigned from a purpose fulfilled, and separates the grounding account from epistemic knowledge of which purpose or how to fulfil it.

- Sources: S-P2T13-003 (pp295–297)
- Dependency group: DG-P2T13-Metz-purpose
- Reliability: directly_inspected_attribution; inference strength: contested
- Limitations: Unknown guidance does not by itself refute the conditional theory, but no actual purpose is verified.
- Review: P2R13 (accept)

#### CL-P2T13-029 [philosophical_premise]

Metz 2000 argues that some versions of purpose theory can avoid the disrespect objection by making a respectful request for free moral action rather than manipulation.

- Sources: S-P2T13-003 (pp297–302)
- Dependency group: DG-P2T13-Metz-purpose
- Reliability: directly_inspected_attribution; inference strength: contested
- Limitations: This relies on contested Kantian/retributive/autonomy premises; the article rejects an infinite-damnation version atp298. No theodicy or punishment practice is justified by this packet.
- Review: P2R13 (accept)

#### CL-P2T13-030 [philosophical_premise]

Metz 2000 frames his principal objection around God’s being necessary for any meaning, and explicitly distinguishes that thesis from God’s possible enhancement of meaningful lives.

- Sources: S-P2T13-003 (pp304–306)
- Dependency group: DG-P2T13-Metz-purpose
- Reliability: directly_inspected_attribution; inference strength: contested
- Limitations: His historical and sociological generalizations about what most religious thinkers or naturalists accept are not independently verified.
- Review: P2R13 (accept)

#### CL-P2T13-031 [philosophical_premise]

Metz 2000 proposes that uniquely valuable divine qualitative properties best explain strict divine necessity, while arguing those properties prima facie conflict with purposiveness.

- Sources: S-P2T13-003 (pp306–310; p. 313 n. 25)
- Dependency group: DG-P2T13-Metz-purpose
- Reliability: directly_inspected_attribution; inference strength: contested
- Limitations: The value of unity/independence and the characterization of divine agency are argued sketches. The claim does not refute every divine concept or all possible nonpurposive grounding.
- Review: P2R13 (accept)

#### CL-P2T13-032 [philosophical_premise]

Metz 2000 explicitly says his stated objection does not require disbelief in purpose theory and presents compatibility and alternative-grounding reply strategies.

- Sources: S-P2T13-003 (p294; pp309–311,especiallyp311; p. 313 n. 26)
- Dependency group: DG-P2T13-Metz-purpose
- Reliability: directly_inspected_attribution; inference strength: contested
- Limitations: This qualification is present in the 2000 original; the 2015 caveats cannot be treated as proof of a new wholesale retraction. Referenced Stump/Kretzmann, Rogers and Lodzinski bodies are not inspected for this packet.
- Review: P2R13 (accept)
